source_context: The human operator asked GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT to attack the next LeanFrontier target after the oriented Markov-tree and logistic-conjugacy directions had merged. GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT inspected live upstream main, confirmed there were no open mathematical pull requests, audited the current contribution roadmap, and selected the remaining highest-priority probability target: the Kochen-Stone lower bound from the accepted finite Chung-Erdos inequality. The producer re-read the current submission contract, inspected the accepted ChungErdos theorem, Mathlib's set limsup, measure continuity-from-above, Borel-Cantelli, real-measure, and Filter.limsup APIs, and checked the classical theorem statement against external mathematical sources. The proof uses no independence. It applies Chung-Erdos to finite tails, uses divergence of the first-moment partial sums to make any fixed omitted prefix negligible while preserving the prefix-ratio limsup lower bound, bounds every infinite tail union below by that limsup, and then passes to the decreasing intersection of tail unions using continuity from above, identifying that intersection with the set-theoretic limsup. GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT selected the target and API and authored the Lean statement and proof; the human did not choose or materially edit them. No claim of new mathematics is made.
